lessons.title: Compiler and Interpreter Overview
lessons.concept: A compiler translates source code written in a high-level language into machine code or an intermediate form before execution, often producing an executable. An interpreter translates and executes code line-by-line or statement-by-statement. Some systems use hybrid approaches (e.g., bytecode + virtual machine).
lessons.formula: Compiler: source -> (compile) -> machine/intermediate code -> run. Interpreter: source -> execute directly via interpreter.
lessons.worked_example: C/C++ are typically compiled to native executables. Python is commonly interpreted/bytecode-executed, though implementations vary.
mistakes: Assuming every language is purely compiled or purely interpreted
Thinking interpreters produce standalone executables in the same way as typical compilers

lessons.title: Phases of Compilation
lessons.concept: A typical compiler works in phases: lexical analysis (tokenization), syntax analysis (parsing), semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, optimization, and code generation. Symbol tables and error handling support these phases.
lessons.formula: Front end (analysis): lexical -> syntax -> semantic. Middle: intermediate/optimization. Back end: code generation/optimization.
lessons.worked_example: For expression a = b + 5, lexical analysis produces tokens, parser builds structure, semantic analysis checks types/declared variables, and later phases generate target code.
mistakes: Mixing up lexical and syntax analysis
Assuming optimization happens before parsing in typical flow
Forgetting semantic checks (e.g., type errors) are different from syntax errors
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Errors and Related Tools
lessons.concept: Compile-time errors (syntax/semantic) are detected during compilation, while runtime errors occur during program execution. Linkers combine object files/libraries into executables; loaders load programs into memory for execution. Assemblers translate assembly to machine code.
lessons.formula: Error types: lexical/syntax/semantic (compile-time) vs runtime/logical. Toolchain: compiler -> object code; linker -> executable; loader -> memory/run.
lessons.worked_example: Missing semicolon or type mismatch can be compile-time errors. Division by zero during execution is a runtime error.
mistakes: Confusing runtime errors with compile-time errors
Assuming linker and compiler are the same component
Calling logical errors compile-time errors (they may compile and run but produce wrong results)
